findings.title: Role-mapping checks ignore manage-clients admins
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission and never treat AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS as sufficient. This class fully replaces ClientPermissions whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and V1 granted those operations to holders of manage-clients (including master-realm and realm admins) before any fine-grained policy was consulted. canManage and canManageClientScopes still short-circuit on that role, so the same admin can update a client but is denied mapping client roles, composite roles, and client-scope roles. Admin console role-mapping calls fail with 403 even when no FGAP policy was meant to restrict that admin. The new tests only cover a user without manage-clients, so they do not catch this.

findings.title: Per-client resource hides all-clients allow and deny
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) loads the object resource by client id and, if that row exists, evaluates only that resource. The all-clients resource is consulted only when no object resource exists. Creating any object permission (for example VIEW on one client) therefore drops realm-wide grants such as MANAGE/CONFIGURE/MAP_ROLES on "Clients" for that client, so an admin who can manage every client loses manage on any client that also has an object-level permission. The same short-circuit skips a realm-wide negative permission, so a deny-all policy on Clients does not apply to a client that already has an object resource and a positive object permission. Authorization becomes order-dependent and can both lock out legitimate admins and bypass a type-level deny.

findings.title: Missing Clients resource NPEs permission checks
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, hasPermission assigns getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls PolicyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with no null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null if the "Clients" resource was never created. findByResource dereferences that resource and throws NullPointerException, so canView/canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles return 500 instead of false. AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already non-null and never adds the new Clients resource type or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-client-scope, map-roles-composite). Any realm that enabled admin permissions before this schema change keeps the old resource server, so the first per-client check 500s and creating a Clients permission fails because those scopes are absent. init needs an upgrade path, and the evaluator must treat a missing type resource as deny.

findings.title: V2 throws on token exchange and permissions API
findings.body: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now always returns ClientPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, but canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, and getPermissions all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Token exchange calls AdminPermissions.management().clients().canExchangeTo and will fail the request with a server error for every realm that has the feature enabled, even if token-exchange permissions are unused. The admin client management-permissions endpoint calls isPermissionsEnabled, then resource and getPermissions, so opening fine-grained permissions for a client 500s. These methods are still part of the live ClientPermissions contract; they need a V2 behavior (or a safe deny/empty result), not an exception. getEvaluationContext is unused dead code left from an unfinished exchange check.

findings.title: Client permission resources have no display name
findings.body: getResourceName only resolves Users resources to a username. Client object resources are stored under the client UUID (resolveClient returns client.getId()) and getOrCreateResource never sets a display name, so the fallback resource.getDisplayName() is null. Admin APIs that label permission resources will show a blank name for every client permission, and a deleted client is not reported as missing the way a missing user is (ModelIllegalStateException). This method needs a Clients branch that loads the client and returns its clientId, and a defined error if the client is gone.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the type name, not client ids
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every Clients-typed resource that grants the scope. The schema's all-clients resource is named "Clients" (init sets both name and type to the resource type). A user who only has a type-level grant therefore gets a set containing the literal "Clients" rather than every client id, and callers that filter with client.getId() match nothing. Object resources are only included if their type was set to Clients; getOrCreateResource creates them by name and scopes and never calls setType, so per-client grants are also omitted if no other layer sets the type. Listing and role-mapping UIs that rely on this set will hide clients the user is allowed to access. The type resource should be expanded or skipped, and returned ids must be real client ids.

findings.title: Removal listener checks V1 but dispatches V2 clients
findings.body: Cleanup now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled, but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws. If both features are on, ClientRemovedEvent calls the throwing V2 method and client deletion fails. If only V2 is on, the listener does nothing, so the authorization resource created for that client id is never removed. There is no other V2 delete hook in this change, so object-level client permissions are left pointing at deleted clients.

findings.title: requireView javadoc describes a boolean result
findings.body: requireView is void and throws ForbiddenException, but its new javadoc says it returns true if canView() returns true. requireViewClientScopes (line 101) has the same error: it says it returns true if canViewClientScopes() returns true. Callers reading the interface will treat these as predicates instead of enforcing methods. The comments should match requireManage/requireList and state that they throw when the corresponding can* check is false.
